Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for taking this on. A quick summary of SmallBank's immediate needs to inform model selection and sizing:
- Primary features: automated customer support triage (classification + extractive summary), short-form credit-decision rationale generation (one-paragraph, structured), and FAQ retrieval augmentation.
- Typical prompt size: ~700–1,200 tokens (customer history + 3–5 prior messages). Expected model response: 150–350 tokens.
- Expected steady-state traffic: ~50k requests/day (weekdays), with bursts up to ~3k requests/hour during morning peak.
- Latency target: sub-1.5s p95 for triage flows; sub-3s p95 for rationale gen.
- Compliance note: PII redaction must be supported and we need model variant options for private deployment later (VPC).

I've attached our product requirements and a small set of sample prompts. Looking for: model shortlist by 8K/16K context, a ballpark token/day estimate, and any immediate ops ask (caching, prefix KV suggestions). Can we do a short architecture call next week?

Thanks,

Thanks Kim — here's a compact draft for the shortlist and rough sizing. Keeping it conservative for the initial onboarding sprint.

Model shortlist (initial candidates):
- Option A: Llama2-70B-chat (8K / 16K variant) — Pros: strong instruction-following, good for summarization and structured outputs; Cons: larger memory footprint, higher token cost if using float32; recommended quantized FP16/4-bit for hosted.
- Option B: Mistral-Instruct-34B-16K (hypothetical name here for pairing) — Pros: better latency/cost for shorter responses, competitive quality for classification+extractive tasks; Cons: may need more prompt engineering for rationale generation.
- Option C: Redfin-Chat-13B (smaller, optimized) — Pros: much lower cost, good for triage/classification and caching-friendly; Cons: may miss nuance on credit rationale.

Preliminary token math (using Anna's midpoint numbers):
- Avg prompt: 950 tokens; avg response: 250 tokens => ~1,200 tokens per request.
- 50,000 requests/day * 1,200 tokens = 60,000,000 tokens/day (60M).
- Weekday peak: 3,000 requests/hour => 3,000 * 1,200 = 3.6M tokens in peak hour.

Throughput & capacity notes:
- If using hosted API with continuous batching, expect batching to reduce per-token overhead on larger models; however latency SLOs for triage imply we should use small batch windows (20–40ms) and prefer mid-sized models for consistent p95.
- For 16K context and heavy KV cache usage, plan memory budget for KV caches (rough rule: ~0.5–1.5GB per concurrent KV stream depending on model).

Ops recommendations (short):
- Implement prefix caching for common templates (customer details + product context) — assume 30–40% hit rate initially; reduce token cost by reusing cached KV.
- Use a tiered model strategy: Redfin-13B for triage (fast, cheap), Mistral-34B for rationale generation when higher quality needed, Llama2-70B-chat as fallback for hard cases or private deployment.

Next items: Marcus — can you add resource footprints (GPU mem / expected instance types) for these three options? Grace — please sanity-check the 30–40% cache hit assumption against similar banking customers (if we have past comps).

I'll convert this into a single-page summary for Anna once we have Marcus/Grace inputs.

—Monica

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Attached is a short one-pager (and an internal XLSX) with the recommended slate and rough token math. Short summary here:

1) Initial slate (what we'll pilot):

   - High-quality rationale: Mistral-Instruct-34B (8K) — balance of quality and cost for one-paragraph rationales.
   - Escalation/fallback: Llama2-70B-chat (16K) — reserved for complex cases and future private deployment.

2) Token & capacity estimate (midpoint):
   - ~1,200 tokens/request => ~60M tokens/day on weekdays.
   - Peak hour demand ~3.6M tokens.
   - With caching (planned prefix hit 30–40%) token/day could drop to ~36–42M effective tokens/day depending on hit-rate.

3) Ops & configuration asks from our side:

   - For PII: we'll provision a private deployment checklist and a KMS integration plan; compliance team is copied for evidence requests.

4) Next meeting: Wed, 31 Mar at 10am PT — 30m architecture + SLO alignment. We'll run through the one-pager and agree on the initial pilot gates.
